learning_objective: The learner will examine ten heading lines from two page outlines and mark each as fine or as having a skipped level, a second main heading, or a vague heading, with at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** heading-outline-checker
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Analyze
**Bloom Verb:** examine
**Learning Objective:** The learner will examine ten heading lines from two page outlines and mark each as fine or as having a skipped level, a second main heading, or a vague heading, with at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Heading Structure (defined in this chapter above this block) and Headings and Subheadings (defined in Chapter 6). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each heading line the learner commits one of four options. A choice is correct when it matches the Correct option column in Content. Mastery is at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt. Reading the defect definitions is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A heading level is chosen for how large it looks. (2) A page may have several main headings. (3) A short heading is a good heading. **Instructional Rationale:** Examining an outline is an Analyze-level action, because the learner must compare each line with the line before it and with the page's structure. Ten lines with three different defects teach the learner to look for each defect separately. **Content:** The four options: Fine, Skipped level, Second main heading, Vague heading. The two outlines (each line shows the heading level and text): | Outline | Line | Level | Text | Correct option | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | A | A1 | h1 | Watershed Basics | Fine | The one main heading names the page. | | A | A2 | h2 | What a watershed is | Fine | It sits directly under the main heading and says what follows. | | A | A3 | h4 | Parts of a watershed | Skipped level | It jumps from h2 to h4 and skips h3. | | A | A4 | h2 | How water moves | Fine | It returns to the section level and says what follows. | | A | A5 | h3 | Runoff | Fine | It sits directly under an h2 and names its topic. | | B | B1 | h1 | Rivers | Fine | The one main heading names the page. | | B | B2 | h2 | Where rivers start | Fine | It sits directly under the main heading and says what follows. | | B | B3 | h1 | River safety | Second main heading | A page should have one main heading, and this line starts a second. | | B | B4 | h2 | Stuff | Vague heading | The word does not tell the reader what the section holds. | | B | B5 | h3 | Cold water | Fine | It sits under an h2 and says what follows. | **Provenance:** The outlines are made up for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The defects follow the chapter section "Heading Structure". **Rules:** Each line has exactly one correct option. Seven lines are Fine, and the three defects each occur once. A line is a Skipped level when its level is more than one deeper than the previous line's level. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees outline A as an indented list with levels shown. 2. The learner chooses an option for each line, and the choice is committed. 3. The sim shows whether each choice was correct and the Why text. 4. The learner repeats for outline B. 5. After line B5 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 10 lines in outline order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [option]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This line is [option]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 10 correct on the first attempt". At 9 or more it adds "You can read a page's outline." Below 9 it lists the Why text of each missed line. **Starting State:** Outline A with no choices made. The question shown is "Is this heading fine?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter says a page should have one main heading with subheadings nested in order and no skipped level, and that headings should describe their sections.
